extraction.Name: Bessie Martin
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee at the time she accepted it, but was told that it was necessary for her to take it, and she did so
extraction.Buyer: J. W. Good, of Chadron, Nebraska, for $1000.00, cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she was back on taxes, knew that she could not meet future taxes, and thought best to take what she could get
extraction.Occupation/Income: she and her family is supported by her husband, who has poor health, but he farms her home place, and occasionally works for a neighbor, and this is the source of his income
extraction.NOTES: mentally incompetent, has poor health, having stomach trouble and rheumatism; has four minor children to support; has never received any help from the County or the Government; document number 7584; sworn November 20, 1928 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
